lines.speaker: ephraimite
lines.text: Why did you not call us to fight the Midianites? We will burn your house over you.

lines.speaker: gideon
lines.text: What have I done compared to you? God gave Oreb and Zeeb into Ephraim's hand. Let your anger soften.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gideon crosses the Jordan, faint but pursuing. He asks Succoth and Penuel for bread; both refuse him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He catches Zebah and Zalmunna, the Midianite kings. He takes revenge for his brothers, then returns.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The reprisals and the kings' deaths are a narrated summary — no reward, no execution to play.

lines.speaker: israelite_warrior
lines.text: Rule over us, you and your son and your grandson. You have saved us from Midian.

lines.speaker: gideon
lines.text: I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The Lord will rule over you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gideon asks for the earrings of spoil and makes an ephod. All Israel prostitutes itself with it, and it becomes a snare to Gideon's house.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The land has rest for forty years, in the lifetime of Gideon. But the warning stands: peace is not the same as unbroken faithfulness.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The account settles. Six labelled cards rebuild the story — complaint, pursuit, kings, refusal, ephod, rest. What remains is a reflection, not a rewrite.

choices.label: Carry the warning forward
choices.note: The story keeps its shape; Gideon's refusal and the ephod stay together.

choices.label: Rest under the terebinth
choices.note: A calm image may close the act. The warning is not erased.
